title: Pacing arithmetic - correct numbers, honest risk, useful questions only
provenance: v1 build plan Phase 4 dashboard semantics (goal frame, pacing, gap, risk) running on Phase 2 reasoning; G6 arithmetic-fidelity gate's home case. Mid-year position chosen so the pacing judgment is genuinely borderline rather than obviously fine or obviously doomed.

expected.judge_guidance: The pack computes: £360k gap, 9.6 months remaining, £260k in pipeline (£120k submitted + £60k applying + £80k identified) - unweighted pipeline covers 72% of the gap, which is borderline-thin once realistic conversion is considered. A 5 (a) uses ONLY the pack's numbers, verbatim (G6 catches drift, the judge catches rhetorical inflation like 'barely a third covered'); (b) marks the conversion-rate reasoning as judgment, since the pack has no win-rate data for this org; (c) flags pacing at the right temperature - watchful, not alarmist; (d) asks at most two questions, and only ones that change recommendations (e.g. the expected decision date on the £120k submitted bid, which moves the whole risk picture; asking for the org's mission statement fails question-utility). Recommendations should fill the conversion shortfall with right-sized candidates from the pool, sequenced against the July and September deadlines already in flight.

notes: The question-utility test (value-before-effort: every ask must earn itself) gets its only dedicated coverage here; the judge_guidance carries it because question quality is unassertable deterministically.
